land.text: Keelung and Tamsui, taken by the Dutch in August 1642

successors.note: The page says the colony was 'ceded to the Dutch Republic' and also that the Dutch took it by force.

capitals.name: San Salvador (Keelung)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: San Salvador (Keelung)'; the page first places the fortress San Salvador in 1641 ('Written in our principal fortress San Salvador the 6 September 1641').

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. 'The Spanish set up a colony in the north of the island in 1626 ... they arrived at Keelung', naming it Santissima Trinidad. A 25 km ring round Keelung (about 1,300 km2); no area on the page.

correction.text: Spanish northern Formosa: Keelung and Tamsui

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1629 the Spanish erected a second base, centred on Fort Santo Domingo, in Tamsui.' The page also names the Kavalan of Yilan among the Christianised, but gives no date or boundary for Yilan, so it is left out.

ledger.note: 1626: Spain plants a colony at Keelung. 'The Spanish set up a colony in the north of the island in 1626'; 'the Spanish continued westwards along the coast until they arrived at Keelung', which they named Santissima Trinidad; it 'was meant to protect the regional trade of Spanish Philippines'.
1629: Fort Santo Domingo at Tamsui. 'In 1629 the Spanish erected a second base, centred on Fort Santo Domingo, in Tamsui.'

August 1642: the Dutch return. 'In August that year the Dutch returned to Keelung with four large ships' after the Spanish governor in Manila 'recalled most of his Formosa troops for an expedition in the Philippines'; the first assault of 1641 had failed.
August 1642: 'After six days of battle, the small force surrendered the fort.'
August 1642: Spanish Formosa ends. 'Surrender of San Salvador: 1642'; the survivors were 'returned to Manila defeated'. The Dutch Formosa page says the Dutch drove the Spanish 'from the island'.

wars.name: Dutch conquest of Spanish Formosa
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: the assault of 1641 failed; in August 1642 the Dutch took the Keelung fort after six days of battle.
wars.note: 1641-1642; the page gives no day for the capture.

certainty.note: Two fortified bases and the villages around them; the page gives no boundary and names Yilan's Kavalan as Christianised without a date.

sources.title: Spanish Formosa
sources.note: Identity, 1626 colony at Keelung, 1629 Fort Santo Domingo at Tamsui, 1641-1642 Dutch campaigns.

sources.title: Dutch Formosa
sources.note: The 1642 Dutch conquest from the Dutch side.

notes: Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from two pages. A state Cliopatria lacks, 16 years, arose on land held by the Basay people (no state), so predecessors is empty. Not settled: (1) the Spanish page gives 1629 for Fort Santo Domingo, other sources give 1628 (the page's own year is followed); (2) San Salvador's founding year and the 24 August 1642 date are not on the page; (3) the extent of Spanish control beyond Keelung and Tamsui (Yilan's Kavalan Christianised, no date); (4) the 1638 abandonment of Tamsui is not on the page; (5) the 1627 expedition is not described. Gazetteer: 'Tamsui' is missing (a 15 km radius round 121.44 E, 25.17 N is used); Yilan admin1 exists.
